Commentary.Commentary: New Zealand will be top of the moon right now. How good were they with the ball? The pacers ruled with some swing bowling display. Matt Henry and Henry Shipley started the proceedings and then Daryl Mitchell came in to get three wickets to his name while the other two mentioned too ended with three each. They were superb in the slips and overall on the field as well. This should be an easy chase for New Zealand unless Sri Lanka come up with some magic. Stay tuned.

A sorry looking batting card for the Lankans. They were beaten by pace dearly. There was no significant contributions from anyone apart from Nissanka at the top. The other batters were victims to some class swing bowling. They were right under the pump as they lose three inside the 10 overs. Dasun Shanaka and Pathum Nissanka were trying to build a stand but a silly run out didn't help them. The skipper and Chamika Karunaratne made some handy contributions but we feel, this is way below-par.
OUT! BOWLED! That is it! This is full and slanting on middle. Rajitha looks to drive but gets an inside edge and it deflects onto the stumps. Sri Lanka are bowled out for 157.

Hello and welcome to the final ODI of this series as the Kiwis take on the Lankans. This has been an entertaining series with evenly fought by both teams. New Zealand took the lead in the first game while the second one was washed out due to rain. The forecast is not so good here as well but let’s hope for the best. Toss and team news coming up.
...Match Day...

It is now time for the third and final ODI match between New Zealand and Sri Lanka. We have come a long way in this series, but there is still more to come as these two teams will shift their attention to the shortest format after this one. So, as things stand it is the Kiwis that lead this series 1-0, thanks to the rain gods, as the second match got washed out without even a ball being bowled. This is Sri Lankan's final opportunity to level the series and this Sri Lankan side certainly does not give up till the very last ball. Even though they suffered a comprehensive defeat in the first ODI, they certainly have the talent to overcome the mishap. The visitors would hope they can pick things up with the bat in hand and focus on building stands in the middle this time around. The Kiwis though are using this opportunity to fine-tune some youngsters by offering them game time and see how they progress, ahead of the World Cup. The hosts would simply to eyeing to seal the ODI series. Expect nothing less than a cracker. Which team will get over the line? We shall find out together.
